function: SecureLink-DDPG selects IRS phase shifts, information/AN power split, NOMA power allocation, EH factors, and sample counts to maximize secrecy sum rate (p. 8).
system: Semi-passive reflecting IRS, 8 elements (up to 16), serves two NOMA users plus an eavesdropper; OFDM, SWIPT; BS antennas and carrier band not stated (pp. 4, 9-10).
method: DDPG deep RL (SecureLink-DDPG): actor and critic with two hidden layers of 128 neurons, trained by reinforcement learning with replay memory; stable after 350 episodes (pp. 8, 12-13).
data_channel: Custom simulator: Rician channels (K=10) for BS-IRS, IRS-user, IRS-eavesdropper links, path-loss exponent 2, 1,000 Monte Carlo runs; no standard model or measured data (pp. 4, 10).
test_conditions: Same simulator for training and results; distances, Pt, and 6 or 8 IRS elements varied per result; no stated transfer to an unseen setting (pp. 10, 13-14).
baselines: Non-learned: discretized grid-based search (GBS) with step 0.1 and IRS phase step 2pi/8; no learned baseline compared (pp. 13-14).
metrics: Secrecy sum rate and per-user secrecy rates, harvested energy, reward convergence over episodes, DDPG versus GBS gain percent, computational complexity in FLOPS (pp. 10-14).
complexity: FLOPS expressions for DDPG training and steady state (Eqs. 34-40) versus GBS (Eq. 41); DDPG uses 1.292e-3 % of GBS resources at 8 IRS elements (pp. 9-10, 13).
q1_support: p. 10: "are modeled as Rician channels with Rician factors K1 = K2 = 10". Custom Rician simulator (Eqs. 1-4 on p. 4); no 3GPP model, DeepMIMO, or measured data is mentioned.
q2_support: p. 13: "These numerical results are obtained for a particular set of distance values". Tables I-II and Fig. 16 vary distances and IRS elements; the paper never states that a trained agent is tested on a scenario unseen in training.
q3_support: p. 13: "contrast the secure sum rates and energy harvesting levels produced by the SecureLink-DDPG method with those achieved using the GBS method". GBS is non-learned; no earlier learned method or standard learning algorithm is compared.
q4_support: p. 9: "number of training iterations multiplied by the number of floating-point operations" (Eqs. 34-40 give FLOPS for training and steady state); p. 13: DDPG uses 1.292e-3 % of the GBS resources at 8 IRS elements.
q5_support: p. 10: "are modeled as Rician channels with Rician factors K1 = K2 = 10", own simulated channels. No code or data link, public dataset, or availability statement appears in pp. 1-15; the only URLs are reference entries.
notes: Includes with area 3 as a judgment for the reviewer: the learned decision is the IRS phase-shift matrix, with power split, NOMA allocation, and EH factors, and the goal is secrecy sum rate. Physical-layer security is not in the excluded functions list. BS and user antenna counts are not stated; the RIS is present, so the system check passes. Tables I-II and Fig. 16 were read as images of pp. 13-14.
